newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fed's McDonough confident HK can manage US$ peg.
newsitem.headline: Fed's McDonough confident HK can manage US$ peg.

text.p: New York Federal Reserve Bank president William McDonough said on Tuesday he was confident of Hong Kong's ability to manage its currency's peg to the U.S. dollar through the territory's reversion to China next year.

"The degree of success that Hong Kong has had managing the dollar should continue in future, and I don't think the transition has anything to do with it," McDonough told a conference in Hong Kong sponsored by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's defacto central bank.
The Hong Kong dollar is pegged at HK$7.80 to US$1.00.

China, which resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong at midnight, June 30, 1997, has promised to allow the HKMA to persue an independent monetary policy beyond the handover and to maintain the U.S. dollar peg.
